source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
source.author: Francesco Orabona

definitions.simplexGammaProduct: literal real product using real powers, including 0^0=1
definitions.nonnegativeMassSimplex: literal nonnegative coordinates with fixed sum

inventory.text: The product, the nonnegative simplex and the convention 0^0=1.
Take logarithms and define the scalar h.
Compute h second derivative using Proposition A.10(f).
Use convexity of the reciprocal-square kernel and integral Jensen on each unit cell.
Sum the cell bounds, evaluate the half-line integral as 1/x and deduce nonnegative curvature.
Extend the log sum continuously to the closed simplex, including zero coordinates.
Use convexity on the simplex to attain the maximum at an extreme point.

alternative_routes.lean_route: The same unit-cell comparison follows from the evaluated primitive and algebraic midpoint bound. Both the interval and half-line integrals are proved.

bookkeeping: Finite coordinate and vertex sum evaluation
